thread:
Priya (ml-onboard): Hey team — bringing up Cassia v1.2 (7B) for embed/serve. License includes a clause about 'persistent attribution for derivative distributions' — unsure how that maps to quantized variants we might ship. @Nora can you eyeball?
Ben (infra): Quick infra question: if we serve the quantized model from Hosted API, that's internal only. If we hand over a container or on-device bundle, that's redistribution, right?
Nora (legal): Short answer: yes. Hosting-only (no weights transferred) is generally allowed; handover of images/artifacts counts as distribution. Need to review exact wording.
Priya (ml-onboard): Copying the clause we got from the model card: "Adapters, derivatives, or quantized variants must include a persistent attribution file 'ATTRIBUTION.txt' and retain original license headers in weight metadata when distributed."
Kori (devx): For Dedicated customers we sometimes deliver an OCI image that contains the model weights — that'll be distribution. For Hosted we keep weights server-side. So different obligations in each flow.
Ben (infra): Practically, can we satisfy "persistent attribution" by placing ATTRIBUTION.txt in the runtime image filesystem rather than embedding it into the weight blob?
Nora (legal): Yes, if you distribute the runtime image containing weights, attribution in the image filesystem is acceptable. The key is it must accompany the distributed artifact and be persistent/readable. Also want a registry record.
Priya (ml-onboard): Would a tiny manifest.json with a pointer to the full attribution hosted on our docs site be enough?
Nora (legal): Prefer both: include full ATTRIBUTION.txt in the artifact and a machine-readable manifest with metadata (license, original model id, provenance URL). That reduces ambiguity during audits.
Priya (ml-onboard): On quantization specifics — some quantizers change tokenization alignment (we saw off-by-one subtoken mapping). Does that count as a derivative that needs extra attribution?
Kori (devx): If you modify tokenizer files or vocab, that's a modification of upstream assets — it is a derivative. Pure numerical transform of weights is still a derivative but often treated differently; when tokenizer changes, it's definitely a new artifact.
Ben (infra): We also have a workflow where we strip unused vocab to save space for edge bundles. That modifies tokenizer — seems risky.
Nora (legal): Correct — any modification to tokenizer or vocab triggers derivative obligations. For on-device/offline bundles we should mark them for formal legal signoff.
Priya (ml-onboard): Sounds like action items. Also need clearance to run quant eval releases — who signs off on packaging for customer deliverables?
Nora (legal): I'll draft a short checklist for model-onboard packaging: 1) Hosted API: register model card + license in model registry, include link to ATTRIBUTION on registry. 2) Dedicated (delivered image): include ATTRIBUTION.txt in image root, machine-readable manifest, and update delivery contract terms. 3) On-device/offline packages: require formal Legal review and audit trail.
Kori (devx): I'll add a checkbox to the onboarding form: "Distributes weights or runtime (OCI/edge bundle)" that triggers Legal review workflow.
Priya (ml-onboard): For evaluation: Sasha, can you run baseline FP16 vs 4-bit quant and tokenizer-slim experiments and report quality delta? We'll gate shipping on <2% drop for our core benchmarks.
Sasha (ml-evals): On it. Will run a small, reproducible harness — fp16 -> 4bit post-training quant, and tokenizer-slim (vocab prune) variant. Expect ~1-3% dev loss depending on task. Will post PR with numbers.
Ben (infra): If Legal says we must include ATTRIBUTION in delivered images, we should add a build step to inject ATTRIBUTION.txt and manifest into OCI layers and sign them. I can prototype that.
Priya (ml-onboard): Also want to capture provenance metadata in our model registry: original checkpoint hash, quantizer config, tokenizer diff patch id.
Nora (legal): Good. That provenance info helps satisfy attribution and auditability. I'll open LR ticket.
legal-bot: Nora submitted Legal Review request LR-2026-342: "Cassia v1.2 distribution & quantization packaging". Status: queued.
Priya (ml-onboard): Thanks — we'll pause packaging until LR done. Kori, Ben: can you add the onboarding flags and an image-injection prototype?
Kori (devx): Yep, will add flag and link to checklist.
Ben (infra): I'll prototype OCI injection and layer signing by EOD tomorrow.
Priya (ml-onboard): Great. Sasha, ping here when evals are done and include the small runbook so Legal can see exact modifications.
Sasha (ml-evals): Will do.
Nora (legal): I'll follow up with the checklist doc and update the model-onboard playbook. Thanks everyone.
